sourceQualifiedTimeline.title: First Choir formation and assault — contested timing
sourceQualifiedTimeline.sourceFinding: The original presents unnamed chords, invitation/formation and active seal repair before the direct scarlet-fire assault opening the Sundering. The owner says the First Choir arose in response to Asmodeus attacking Calanthir.
sourceQualifiedTimeline.currentLimit: Owner intent is recorded; exact event/awakening timing remains unresolved. Do not restore the withdrawn no-agency-before-assault or one-to-one Harmony mapping.

sourceQualifiedTimeline.title: Pillar realms mature after the Sundering
sourceQualifiedTimeline.sourceFinding: The Planes Ascendant opening explicitly follows the Sundering and describes four differentiating realms; the next chapter begins with all four contributing to the Weave.
sourceQualifiedTimeline.currentLimit: This is relative narrative order, not a numbered-year or floor mapping.

sourceQualifiedTimeline.title: Watch Convocation and aspirant gates
sourceQualifiedTimeline.sourceFinding: During the Lucent Interregnum, nascent divinity leads the Choir to open access to seven long-vacant Thrones. A gate appears at an unnamed Mirrorsage monastery library.
sourceQualifiedTimeline.currentLimit: The Thrones are described as older than this opening. The monastery has no supplied numbered floor; current gate availability is not selected.

sourceQualifiedTimeline.title: Candescent Loom and Weave refraction
sourceQualifiedTimeline.sourceFinding: After the Argent Gate shines, the narrative describes small acts leaving visible intention records, called the Candescent Loom.
sourceQualifiedTimeline.currentLimit: A source episode does not automatically make every intention visible through current spells or provide a universal moral detection rule.

sourceQualifiedTimeline.title: Pact sentience
sourceQualifiedTimeline.sourceFinding: Accumulated resonance gives the Pact a will distinct from a god or Choir chord in the narrative.
sourceQualifiedTimeline.currentLimit: Do not use this development to identify the Heartcell builder or assign a calendar date.

sourceQualifiedTimeline.title: Archon sites and living records
sourceQualifiedTimeline.sourceFinding: Within the Pact-sentience chapter, Valcendyr forms the Oath Archive in Crystal Bastion and Quorilith establishes Library of Shifting Sigils.
sourceQualifiedTimeline.currentLimit: These are source-established events, with no chosen present-campaign access or Equation holdings.

sourceQualifiedTimeline.title: Shardfall and Silver Prism Year
sourceQualifiedTimeline.sourceFinding: The Moment of First Scatter is called Shardfall; the ensuing Silver Prism Year has elastic length measured by transformed lives. Sixth Archive cartographers meet at Sigil Navigators Library.
sourceQualifiedTimeline.currentLimit: Do not convert the Year into one standard 400-day year or treat Sixth Archive as Floor 6. The library alias remains unresolved.

sourceQualifiedTimeline.title: Epoch of Chosen Threads
sourceQualifiedTimeline.sourceFinding: The Silver Prism Year closes; scholars call the transition the Epoch of Chosen Threads. Community story keys can manifest resource-bearing Dungeon enclaves in the source.
sourceQualifiedTimeline.currentLimit: Epoch terminology supplies no fixed elapsed duration or automatically usable new portal mechanic.

sourceQualifiedTimeline.title: Counter-expression and Unbound Academy
sourceQualifiedTimeline.sourceFinding: The Matrix broadcast prompts the Spiral Integral counter-expression. Quiet Wells later collapse and the Matrix equation fades; after the Sunrise of Chosen Threads a council builds the Unbound Academy.
sourceQualifiedTimeline.currentLimit: The narrative subsequently develops a renewed threat; this episode is not proof that all Oblivion danger has permanently ended or that Academy access is guaranteed now.

sourceQualifiedTimeline.title: Quiet Masquerade and Citadel of Many Echoes
sourceQualifiedTimeline.sourceFinding: Following the Masquerade confrontation, the Academy and Yieldheart guilds build the Citadel at Crystalfall Summit. Its galleries preserve songs, prototypes and restricted chronicles; later the Matrix develops deliberate calculus.
sourceQualifiedTimeline.currentLimit: Do not merge the Citadel with a numbered dungeon floor or assume Selene’s foundation journal is freely accessible.

sourceQualifiedTimeline.title: Matrix Horizon and imminent campaign
sourceQualifiedTimeline.sourceFinding: The Dawn Loom concert identifies the approaching Matrix Horizon. A later chapter places its arrival on the twentieth eve after the Citadel Vigil.
sourceQualifiedTimeline.currentLimit: The passage gives a relative marker, not a bridge to AE dating. Do not equate the Vigil with the Citadel’s founding date without evidence.

sourceQualifiedTimeline.title: High Chancel ascent
sourceQualifiedTimeline.sourceFinding: The fellowship ascends a ladder of living light toward the High Chancel to confront the Matrix edge.
sourceQualifiedTimeline.currentLimit: The route is not a normal descent to Floor 97 or Floor 100 merely because the same saga discusses the Dungeon.

sourceQualifiedTimeline.title: Silent Library and Final Ledger
sourceQualifiedTimeline.sourceFinding: Inside the Matrix, the Silent Library tries to reduce cognition to zero. Memory-rope and song stabilize its books; the Final Ledger is answered and blanks before the walls open onward.
sourceQualifiedTimeline.currentLimit: Keep the encounter’s transformation. An untouched reusable library, a fixed floor or guaranteed access is not supplied.

sourceQualifiedTimeline.title: Shard of Absolute Rest, victory and Charter
sourceQualifiedTimeline.sourceFinding: The black Shard of Absolute Rest splits; the Matrix curve scatters and Null breaches seal. The Charter of Infinite Yield follows. Ul nak’s dream recedes rather than vanishing; Stillness may try again in ages.
sourceQualifiedTimeline.currentLimit: Do not identify this shattered shard with Q6’s focusing crystal, or convert receding dream into death of the survivor/Old God. No identity bridge is established.

sourceQualifiedTimeline.title: Explicit post-Proof-War epilogue
sourceQualifiedTimeline.sourceFinding: Movement One explicitly places its scene after the Proof War. Later movements give the Spiral cosmograph and Choir chorus around the Charter.
sourceQualifiedTimeline.currentLimit: The document’s later setting does not select the current campaign epoch. Map symbols and coils are not numbered dungeon floors.

sourceQualifiedTimeline.title: Epilogue toolbox and express portability
sourceQualifiedTimeline.sourceFinding: Dungeon seeds are headed after Infinite Yield, and three arcs continue beyond the epilogue. P324 expressly permits tables and relics to be used independently of the saga or in multi-era campaigns.
sourceQualifiedTimeline.currentLimit: Preserve both original placement and permission to adapt. Portability does not choose a floor, public truth, chronology or automatic mechanical replacement. Reuse the existing seventeen EPI groups.

equationOperationalRelation.sourceConnection: The supplied Matrix source says difference/choice/memory/conflict produce resonance and that the Matrix tends toward elimination of distinction; this route authors one local engineering manifestation of that theme.
successfulUnderstanding: Recognize the local indicators and authenticated states.
Predict whether a given local test is trending toward stable separated operation or the quiet/abort condition.
Use the documented abort before key seating in this one regulator family.
Explain why convergence is dangerous operational knowledge at a bounded mechanism level.
doesNotAuthorize: No original/lost Equation symbols, coefficients, derivation, or fragment.

cantorWitnesses.text: When the paired voices differ, the regulator carries the strain away from the quiet face. When both voices answer alike, the quiet face brightens and the keeper withdraws the key.
cantorWitnesses.provenance: Original vellum leaf, stitched into an older Choir-maintenance ledger; same hand throughout; abrasion crosses text and binding thread.
cantorWitnesses.authTest: History DC15: binding/ink wear establishes this leaf predates the two recopies; no absolute AE date.

cantorWitnesses.text: Keep difference between the answering tones. Equal answers feed the hush. If the third mark pales, cease the trial before the key completes its turn.
cantorWitnesses.provenance: Tone-stone rubbing on thin vellum, signed by a Cantor office mark also present on the bilingual index.
cantorWitnesses.authTest: Religion DC15: office mark is a liturgical maintenance office mark, not a divine revelation seal.

cantorWitnesses.text: Trial 6: left channel rose, right channel lagged, quiet face dark. Trial 7: channels converged; quiet face lit; manual abort returned both channels to idle. No fourth state observed.
cantorWitnesses.provenance: Numbered inspection sheet with continuous page fibers and a physical puncture pattern matching the Archive binder.
cantorWitnesses.authTest: History or Engineering DC15: sheet is an original inspection record, not a teaching transcription.

cantorWitnesses.text: Copy for novices: Difference keeps the machine awake; sameness wakes the quiet. Withdraw the key when the third mark pales.
cantorWitnesses.provenance: Explicit colophon: “Copied from R/17-b for novices.” Modern Archive fiber and a different hand.
cantorWitnesses.authTest: History DC10 because the recopy status is explicit; it corroborates transmission but is not an independent underlying observation.

cantorWitnesses.text: Teaching copy of Trial 7: convergence, quiet face, abort, idle. The copied margin after “abort” is torn away.
cantorWitnesses.provenance: Explicit teaching stamp and copied line numbering corresponding to CA-W3.
cantorWitnesses.authTest: History DC10; copied lineage makes it non-independent for duplicate-receipt accounting.

Heat-cycle 18, opening minute 27: marks touch the same groove; quiet face bright; third mark pales. Manual abort before seating returned both marks to their starting grooves.
Heat-cycle 19: with a two-groove separation maintained, load remained stable through minute 31. No abort signal appeared.

regulatorPlate.text: PAIR A / PAIR B / QUIET / ABORT. Do not seat keeper key while QUIET is lit. Abort before the third witness mark empties.

states.idle: PAIR A and PAIR B dark; QUIET dark; keeper key unseated.
states.loaded-separated: PAIR A/B lit with indicator grooves separated by at least one visible groove; QUIET dark or faint; third witness mark steady.
states.converging: indicator grooves approach the same groove; QUIET brightens; third witness mark begins paling.
states.abort-safe: manual ABORT vents load, returns A/B toward idle, locks keeper-key seating for 10 minutes.

regulatorPlate.operationalRelation: NEW PROVISIONAL DESIGN: within this local regulator, preserving a measurable nonzero separation between paired resonance indicators prevents the observed quiet/stillward transition. Convergence to the same indicator groove predicts the quiet-face/abort condition. This relation is local and qualitative; no universal equation coefficient, builder, or Old-One identity is supplied.

nodes.name: Paired Resonance Regulator
nodes.placement: NEW PROVISIONAL mechanism alcove on Floor 68, 12 minutes of ordinary movement beyond the Melted Annex through a maintenance passage
nodes.accessObstacle: A seized inspection grille can be opened by 30 minutes with Engineering and ordinary tools DC15, or by locating WL-PHYS-A and using it as a nonconsumed alignment gauge for automatic opening after 10 minutes. Failure costs the work and leaves grille shut; retry needs repaired tools/new method.
nodes.trigger: After inspection, a researcher may initiate one controlled 90-second load pulse by moving the LOAD lever. This is real execution of the local mechanism, not mere paper analysis.
nodes.cost: 90 seconds world time plus one operator Action to begin in initiative if a scene is active; no RP or spell cost. Manual ABORT is one Action or 6 seconds outside initiative. After any abort, the regulator lockout lasts 10 world-minutes.
nodes.abort: Abort immediately when QUIET is bright and the third witness mark first begins paling, before keeper-key seating. Abort vents the test and returns indicators toward idle; it does not erase observations.
nodes.ignoreAbort: If the party deliberately ignores the authenticated abort point, keeper-seat advances. After 6 additional seconds the regulator slams to QUIET LOCK: local lights extinguish, the access grille seals for 1 hour, all test progress ends, and each creature touching the regulator takes 2d6 force damage (NEW PROVISIONAL local hazard; no extra cosmological effect). No hunter, Old One, Pact enforcement, or death effect is invented by this hazard.
nodes.taint: Paper analysis/Q-ARC-1 that first verifies the dangerous local operational subprinciple = KT1. A supported integrated Functional Model after synthesis = KT2. Performing a preregistered controlled prediction test that demonstrates operational understanding can establish KT3 only after the test’s evidence/result lawfully supports that state. Blind lever pulling is an execution record, not understanding. KT3 episode uses current save/Dazed duration.
nodes.hunt: This local regulator test is not on the current Hunt trigger list merely because it is execution. No Hunt warning/trigger occurs unless the specific contemplated action separately matches an existing Hunt-capable trigger; record warning/commitment/trigger independently.

predictionTests.name: Mechanism-state prediction
predictionTests.episode: Distinct KT3 prediction episode only if the researcher already has KT3-eligible demonstrated understanding; otherwise it is a controlled execution that may become evidence toward KT3 after resolution.

options.A: With indicators held two grooves apart through the pulse, QUIET brightens and abort becomes mandatory.
options.B: With indicators held two grooves apart, QUIET stays dark/faint and no abort signal appears during the 90-second pulse.
options.C: The regulator immediately seats the keeper key regardless of separation.

predictionTests.action: 90-second controlled load pulse with separation fixed at two grooves.
predictionTests.abort: If QUIET unexpectedly brightens or third mark pales, abort immediately; observed deviation falsifies the expected model and ends the test.
predictionTests.outcome: Correct B confirms stable separated-state behavior for this pulse only.

predictionTests.episode: Analysis/prediction; no execution action by itself.

timeline: 09:00 Knowledge Transfer cast; 09:00–10:00 = 60 qualified synthesis minutes.
10:00 loan expires; synthesis pauses at 60/240. Short rest/recovery occurs according to its actual rules and consumes elapsed world time; none of it counts as synthesis.

KT3 save is DC15 WIS Corruption-effect resistance before costs; failure applies actual Dazed until end of next regular turn or 1 minute outside initiative; no decision lock; Dazed immunity leaves no substitute prohibition; no same-episode reroll.
taintAndProtection.PT: No route node automatically creates PT. Only an expressly authored level-5+ qualifying Old-One voice/proximity exposure would. None is authored in this route.

taintAndProtection.Hunt: Knowledge, execution and Hunt are separate ledgers. Present current mechanical warning before any voluntary action that actually matches the precise current Hunt trigger list; taint saves/symptoms are not Hunt triggers. This route adds no hunter roster or new Hunt trigger.
